# Settings

Settings live in `~/.config/termocode/config.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/termocode/config.json`). Change them with **Preferences: Open Settings (UI)**, or edit the file by hand. A missing key uses its default. Unknown keys are kept.

```json
{
  "theme": "vscode-dark-plus",
  "tab_size": 4,
  "word_wrap": true
}
```

## Appearance

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | string | `vscode-dark-plus` | Color theme ID. Same as Preferences: Color Theme. |
| `icons` | enum | `auto` | Icon set: nerd (Nerd Font glyphs), unicode (plain symbols), ascii, or auto (nerd when the terminal bundles Nerd symbols — WezTerm, Ghostty, kitty — or its font setting is a Nerd Font — GNOME Terminal profile, Alacritty, foot; ascii on TERM=linux or a non-UTF-8 locale; else unicode). TERMOCODE_ICON_MODE wins over it. |
| `animations` | enum | `auto` | Overlay / toast / list animations: on, off, or auto (off over SSH and when the terminal is not truecolor). The editor text itself never animates. |
| `images` | enum | `auto` | Inline images (image preview, dashboard logo, Markdown preview): kitty, sixel, blocks (coloured half-blocks, works everywhere with colour), off, or auto (probe the terminal; blocks inside tmux without allow-passthrough). |
| `dashboard_logo` | enum | `text` | The TERMOCODE wordmark on the Welcome page: text (half-blocks, works everywhere), image (a kitty / sixel picture; needs images on), or off. A short window shows a one-line text wordmark instead, so the page fits. |
| `font_delta` | int | `0` | Font size change (points) asked of the terminal at launch and undone on exit; 0 turns it off. Works only in kitty with allow_remote_control on; other terminals (iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty, GNOME, Windows Terminal …) have no way to do it, so use their zoom (Ctrl+-). TERMOCODE_FONT_DELTA wins over it. |

## Editor

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` | bool | `true` | Notify when AI work ends or needs input while the terminal is not focused. Uses the terminal over SSH, or a local desktop helper. |
| `auto_save` | bool | `false` | Save files automatically after edits. |
| `word_wrap` | bool | `false` | Soft-wrap long lines in the editor. |
| `show_hidden` | bool | `false` | Show dot-files in the explorer. |
| `key_hints` | bool | `true` | Show a small popup of the next keys when you press the leader key in the editor and wait a moment. Esc closes it. |
| `tab_size` | int | `4` | Indent width in spaces (1-16). Sets tabstop and shiftwidth. |
| `persistent_session` | enum | `auto` | Run the editor in a background session that survives a dropped connection; run termocode again in the same folder to get it back: on, off, or auto (on over SSH, off locally and inside tmux / screen). Applies the next time termocode starts; --no-session wins over it. |
| `auto_reconnect` | bool | `true` | When the connection to a persistent session drops (network change, Wi-Fi switch, sleep), keep the screen and attach again by itself, also after `termocode ssh` restarts ssh. Keys typed while offline are not sent. Applies the next time termocode starts. |
| `local_history` | bool | `true` | Keep a copy of each file you save (File: Show Local History, File: Recover Deleted File…): 50 versions per file for 30 days, files up to 2 MB, in $XDG_STATE_HOME/termocode/history. Off keeps no new copies. |

## Search

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search_max_results` | int | `2000` | Most results Find in Files shows. 0 means no limit. |

## Git

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git_ai_attribution` | enum | `user` | Who is named on a commit the AI makes (git_commit in the chat, a plan run in a worktree): user (only you), co-author (you, with a Co-authored-by trailer for termocode AI) or ai (termocode AI is the author, you are the committer). |
| `git_auto_fetch` | bool | `false` | Fetch from the remote every 3 minutes in the background while termocode runs (Git: Toggle Auto Fetch). A failed fetch turns it off for this session and says why. |
| `git_issue_link` | string | `(none)` | The web page of an issue key such as ABC-123, with {key} where the key goes (https://tracker.example.com/browse/{key}). A click on a key in a terminal tab opens it. Empty or (none): keys are no links. |
| `git_commit_checks` | bool | `false` | Before each commit, look for large staged files, secret-looking added lines, Windows line endings (CRLF) brought into a file and errors of the Problems list in staged files. A finding asks before the commit (Commit Anyway or Cancel). |
| `git_commit_format` | bool | `false` | Before each commit, format the fully staged files that are open in the editor with their language server and stage the result. A file with unstaged changes too is left as it is. |
| `git_commit_task` | string | `(none)` | Before each commit, run this task (its label, as in Tasks: Run Task). The commit waits; a task that fails asks before the commit. Empty or (none): no task. |
| `git_commit_large_mb` | int | `5` | git_commit_checks: a staged file bigger than this many MB is a finding. |
| `worktree_auto_archive_days` | int | `0` | Archive a worktree with no activity for this many days by itself: its folder goes (git-ignored files like build output too), its branch stays, and x on its row under ARCHIVED brings it back. Only clean worktrees termocode made or you adopted; never pinned ones, ones with changed files or ones an agent works in. Checked when the worktree list is read, at most once an hour. 0 turns it off. |
| `worktree_max` | int | `0` | Most worktrees to keep (the main checkout does not count). When there are more, the oldest clean ones are archived by themselves, by the same rules as worktree_auto_archive_days; one used in the last day is never taken. 0 means no limit. |

## AI

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai_inline` | bool | `true` | Show AI ghost-text completions while typing (needs a configured provider). |
| `ai_next_edit` | bool | `true` | After an edit, show where the AI thinks the next related edit goes (Tab: go there, Tab: apply, Esc: dismiss). Not set: same as ai_inline. |
| `ai_provider` | string | `(auto)` | AI provider: anthropic, openai, openrouter, ollama, lmstudio, openai-compatible, claude-oauth, vertex, bedrock or none. Empty picks anthropic or openai from the API keys it finds. TERMOCODE_AI_PROVIDER overrides it. |
| `ai_model` | string | `(default)` | Chat model ID. Empty uses the provider's default model. |
| `ai_base_url` | string | `(default)` | API base URL, for local or OpenAI-compatible servers. Empty uses the provider's default. |
| `ai_until_done_rounds` | int | `3` | Work until done (the until-done profile, /done, AI: Work Until Done): how many times verify runs at most (1 to 10). A profile's loop.max_rounds wins over it. |
| `ai_until_done_budget_usd` | number | `2.00` | Work until done: the run pauses and asks once its steps have cost this many US dollars. 0 means no budget. A profile's budget_usd wins over it. |

## HTTP

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `http_timeout` | int | `30` | Seconds an HTTP request may take (from .http files, Quick Request and the AI's http_send); # @timeout in a request wins. |
| `http_max_redirects` | int | `10` | Most redirects an HTTP request follows; # @no-redirect in a request shows the 3xx itself. |
| `http_max_body_mb` | int | `20` | Largest HTTP response body read, in MB; a bigger one is cut and marked truncated. |
| `http_ai_max_kb` | int | `32` | Most KB of a response body the AI sees per http_send / http_get_last_response call (it can page on with offset). |
| `http_tls_insecure` | bool | `false` | Skip TLS certificate checks for your own HTTP requests (never for the AI's). Prefer the k retry on the response page, which is per host and per session. |
| `http_cookie_jar` | bool | `true` | Keep cookies between HTTP requests, one jar per environment, saved in http/cookies.json (0600); HTTP: Cookies… shows them; # @no-cookie-jar in a request turns it off for that request. |
| `http_history_max` | int | `200` | Most entries kept in http/history.jsonl. |

## MCP

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp_enabled` | bool | `true` | Offer the tools of the MCP servers in mcp.json to the AI chat. false hides them all without touching mcp.json. |
| `mcp_idle_timeout` | string | `10m` | Stop an MCP server after this long without a tool call (a local one ends, a remote one drops its session); it starts again on the next call. "0" never stops it. A Go duration: 90s, 10m, 1h. |
| `mcp_call_timeout` | string | `60s` | Longest wait for one MCP tool call without an answer or a progress report. A server's "timeout" (seconds) in mcp.json wins. |
| `mcp_max_result_kb` | int | `32` | Cut an MCP tool result to this many KB before the model sees it. |
| `mcp_trust_annotations` | bool | `true` | Let MCP tools the server marks read-only run without asking. false: every MCP tool asks, except the ones in the server's "autoApprove" list. |
| `mcp_oauth_port` | int | `0` | Port of the sign-in listener on 127.0.0.1 for MCP servers with OAuth. 0 takes the first free one of 47391–47395 (the ports termocode's client document lists, so ssh -L 47391:127.0.0.1:47391 works); set another only for an app registered with that port. |
| `mcp_github_client_id` | string | `(built in)` | Client ID of a GitHub OAuth App with Device Flow on, for the GitHub sign-in with a code (Connect a service). Empty uses the one built into termocode (none until it is registered). Not a secret. |
| `mcp_share` | bool | `true` | Run each local MCP server once for all your termocode windows with the same server entry and folder, not once per window. It ends when the last window stops using it (mcp_idle_timeout or quit). false: every window runs its own. Remote servers are not affected. |
| `mcp_log_level` | string | `info` | The lowest level the MCP log (Output: MCP) shows: error, warning, info or debug. Every line is kept, so a lower level shows the older lines too. |
| `mcp_tool_search` | string | `auto` | Send the AI only a search tool instead of every MCP tool's full schema; it loads the tools it needs. auto: only when the MCP tools are big (about 10k tokens). on: always. off: never. |
| `mcp_catalog_url` | string | `(official registry)` | Catalog that AI: MCP: Browse Catalog… reads (an MCP Registry API, for example your team's approved list). Empty: the official MCP Registry. Must be https. |
| `mcp_auto_update` | string | `off` | Servers added from the catalog are pinned to a version. off: check only with AI: MCP: Check for Updates. notify: also check once a day when the MCP servers list opens, and tell. on: the same, and update your own pinned servers (the project file is never changed). |
| `mcp_strict` | bool | `false` | Show a warning row in AI: MCP Servers… under a server whose mcp.json entry has keys termocode does not read (a typo like "comand", or another app's key). Keys that start with _ or $ are comments. |
| `mcp_server` | enum | `auto` | termocode as an MCP server: outside agents (Claude Code, Codex, …) reach a short list of IDE tools (open files, diagnostics, tests, debugger, terminal, git reads and the stash) over a private socket in the session folder, open only to your own user. Tools that change something ask on a card first; files, settings, other git writes and your own MCP servers are never offered. auto: serve once you start an agent tab (F1 → Agent: Start …). on: serve from start. off: never. Applied at once. |

## Updates

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reload_on_new_build` | bool | `true for dev builds, false for releases` | When the termocode program file is replaced by a new build (you rebuilt it), reload into it at the next idle moment, as Reload Window does: unsaved text, the session and the web panel's browser sessions are kept. It waits while an AI turn, an agent or a dialog is busy. Dev builds: on; releases: off. |
| `update_check` | bool | `true` | Look for a newer termocode release once a day, in the background (GitHub, no account needed). A newer one shows a quiet ⬆ chip in the status bar and one toast. Dev builds never look. termocode: Check for Updates works with it off too. |

## Workflows

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflows_enabled` | bool | `true` | Workflows can run: by hand, from the CLI and on their schedules. false stops every schedule and refuses new runs. |
| `workflows_parallel_max` | int | `2` | Most workflow runs at the same time, across all workflows (1-16). A workflow's own parallel setting splits its items inside one run. |
| `workflows_day_budget_usd` | number | `0` | US dollars all workflows may spend on AI in one day; a run that reaches it pauses and asks. 0 means no day budget. |
| `workflows_missed_grace_min` | int | `30` | A scheduled run that was missed (termocode was not running) still runs once if it was due at most this many minutes ago; older ones are recorded as missed. 0 never runs a missed one. |
| `workflows_history_days` | int | `30` | Days a finished workflow run (its file and logs) is kept before it is deleted at start. |
| `workflows_wait_hours` | int | `12` | Hours a run waits for an answer on a card (a write to allow, a budget pause) before the step is marked waiting too long. |
| `workflows_agent_sandbox` | enum | `worktree` | Where an outside agent step works: worktree (it may change files in its own git worktree) or read-only (it may only read). |
| `agent_os_sandbox` | bool | `false` | Outside agents (workflow agent steps, AI run CLI steps, race lanes) run inside an OS sandbox: bwrap on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS. The disk is read-only; only the lane's worktree, the temp folder and the agent's own config folders can be written. The network stays on. No sandbox tool: the agent does not start. |
| `workflows_trigger_poll_min` | int | `5` | Minutes between two looks at GitHub (through gh) for the github triggers of workflows that are on (1-1440). |
| `workflows_webhook_port` | int | `0` | Port on 127.0.0.1 for the inbound webhooks of workflows (POST /hooks/<name>, signed with the secret workflow-hook.<name>). 0 means no webhooks. Put a tunnel or a reverse proxy in front to reach it from outside. |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git_status_blame` | bool | `false` | The status bar shows who last changed the cursor line, and when. Click it to open the commit. Toggle with Git: Toggle Blame in Status Bar. |
| `git_inline_blame` | bool | `false` | Author, age and subject of the cursor line's commit at the end of the line. Toggle with Git: Toggle Inline Blame. |
| `git_line_lens` | bool | `false` | A dim line above the cursor's block (the run of non-blank lines) names who changed it last, when, the commit, and how many authors and commits made it. Toggle with Git: Toggle Line History Lens; Git: Show History of Block lists the block's commits. |
| `git_blame_ignore_whitespace` | bool | `false` | Blame ignores whitespace-only changes (git blame -w). Set with Git: Blame Options…. |
| `git_blame_detect_moves` | bool | `false` | Blame keeps the first commit of lines that were moved or copied (git blame -M -C). Set with Git: Blame Options…. |
| `worktree_dir` | string | `""` | The folder Worktree: New… puts new worktrees in, one folder per branch. Empty: `<repo>.worktrees` next to the repository. `~` is your home folder; a relative path is relative to the repository. Read when the form opens. |

## Databases (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db_max_rows` | int | `10000` | Maximum loaded rows per SQL result (1–100000). Larger results are cut and marked. |
| `db_page_rows` | int | `100` | Rows per SQL result page (1–1000). |
| `db_timeout` | int | `30` | Maximum seconds for a console statement. The session also enforces its own timeout. |
| `db_history_max` | int | `500` | Maximum SQL history entries kept in db/history.jsonl. |
| `db_ai_max_kb` | int | `32` | Maximum size in KB of one AI database tool answer (1–1024). Longer results are cut and marked. |
| `db_redis_separator` | string | `:` | Separator that groups Redis keys into namespaces in the tree (session:ab12 is under session:). Empty: no grouping. |
| `db_redis_max_keys` | int | `10000` | Most Redis keys one tree row loads with SCAN (100–1000000). Past it the row says so; open a namespace to see more. |
| `db_number_format` | string | `(none)` | Pattern for number cells in the result grid, like #,##0.00: a comma groups thousands, after the dot 0 is a digit always shown and # a digit shown when not zero. Empty: as the server sends it. |
| `db_date_format` | string | `(none)` | Pattern for DATE columns, like dd/MM/yyyy (yyyy yy MMM MM dd EEE; text in 'quotes'). Empty: yyyy-MM-dd. |
| `db_time_format` | string | `(none)` | Pattern for timestamps, like yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS XXX (also hh a for 12 hours, z for the zone name). Empty: RFC 3339. |
| `db_time_zone` | string | `(none)` | Zone the grid shows timestamps in: local, UTC or a name like Europe/Berlin. Empty: the zone of each value. |
| `db_bool_style` | enum | `true/false` | How the grid shows boolean cells. |
| `db_alternate_rows` | bool | `false` | Shade every second row of the result grid. |
| `db_lob_bytes` | int | `65536` | Most bytes of one long text or binary cell the grid shows; the rest is cut and the full size is shown. 0: no limit. Copy and export keep the whole value. |
| `db_geometry_format` | enum | `hex` | How the grid shows geometry columns: hex bytes, or WKT text like SRID=4326;POINT(1 2) (WKB, EWKB and MySQL values). |
| `db_exec_mode` | enum | `largest` | What the Run key sends from a .sql file: the whole statement at the caret, the smallest one (a subquery too), it and all after it, or a list to choose from. Set with Databases: Choose Execution Mode…. |
| `db_selection_split` | bool | `true` | Split a selection into statements (true) or send it to the server as one text (false). |
| `db_result_new_tab` | bool | `false` | Each run opens a new result tab and keeps the old ones (up to 9) instead of replacing the tabs that are not pinned. |
| `db_auto_transpose` | bool | `false` | A console result with one row opens flipped: one line per column (t flips it back). |
| `db_row_numbers` | bool | `false` | The result grid shows the row number in front of each row (I on the page turns it on or off). |
| `db_column_types` | bool | `false` | The result grid shows each column's type after its name (T on the page turns it on or off). |
| `db_inline_result` | bool | `false` | After a console run, the first rows of the result show under the statement in the .sql file (Databases: Clear Inline Results removes them). |
| `db_introspect_level` | enum | `auto` | How much a table row in the tree loads: names only, columns, or columns with indexes and foreign keys. auto loads less in schemas with many objects. |
| `db_complete_catalogs` | bool | `false` | SQL completion also offers the system catalogs (pg_catalog, information_schema, sqlite_master…). |
| `db_csv_separator` | string | `,` | Separator of CSV exports: one character, or \t for a tab. |
| `db_csv_header` | bool | `true` | CSV and TSV exports start with a row of column names. |
| `db_csv_null` | string | `(empty)` | Text a NULL cell gets in CSV and TSV exports. |
| `db_export_mask` | string[] | `[]` | Column names (any case; * and ? match) whose values exports, Copy As and Export Tables to Folder write as ••••, for example ["*password*", "email"]. |
| `db_sql_syntax_off` | string[] | `[]` | SQL dialects whose syntax errors the live inspections do not show, for example ["mysql"]. Unknown names and other warnings stay. |

## AI (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai_inline_model` | string | `(provider default)` | Model for inline ghost-text completions. Empty uses a fast model of the provider (for example Claude Haiku or gpt-4.1-mini). |
| `ai_auto_approve` | string[] | `[]` | Agent tool classes that run without asking: fileWrite, git, run, ide, settings, services. Set with AI: Agent Auto-Approve…. |
| `ai_edit_review` | enum | `review` | review: the agent's file changes (write_file, create_file, LSP rename, code actions, format) open as a diff where you accept or reject each change; the agent waits and is told what was written. auto: the old way (a confirm dialog, or no question when fileWrite is auto-approved). Auto-approving fileWrite also skips the review. Toggle with AI: Toggle Edit Review. |
| `ai_review_order` | enum | `explain` | Order of the files in the AI review card (and the web's review cards). explain: the files that explain the change come first: notes and docs, then schemas and the files that define new names, then the code that uses them, tests last; each moved file says why. proposed: the order the agent proposed them in. Toggle with AI: Toggle Review Order. |
| `ai_max_steps` | int | `25` | Most tool steps the AI agent takes for one chat message. At the limit it stops and asks you to send "continue". |
| `ai_prices` | object | `{}` | Model prices in US dollars per million tokens, by model id prefix, over the built-in table (checked 2026-10-18): for example `{"my-model": {"in": 3, "out": 15, "cache_read": 0.3, "cache_write": 3.75}}`. A missing cache price is the input price. Your entry wins over a built-in one. Ollama and LM Studio cost $0; a model with no price shows tokens only. |
| `ai_context_windows` | object | `{}` | Context window in tokens, by model id prefix, over the built-in table: for example `{"qwen2.5-coder": 32768}`. Used for the context % of a turn; a model with no window shows none. |
| `ai_prompt_cache` | enum | `5m` | Prompt cache of Claude (Anthropic key or Claude sign-in). 5m: the tools, the system prompt and the chat so far are cached for 5 minutes, so each next step reads them at a small part of the input price. 1h: the cache lasts an hour (writing it costs more; good when you pause between messages). off: nothing is cached. |
| `ai_reasoning` | enum | `(model default)` | Reasoning level of each new chat and of the main model slot: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (more thinking: better answers on hard problems, slower, more tokens). Empty: the model's default. A slot sets its own with ai_models.<slot>.reasoning. "think" / "ultrathink" in a message raise one turn to high / max; AI: Next Reasoning Level changes it for one chat. |
| `ai_fallback` | string[] | `[]` | Backup models of the main slot, in order: slot names or <provider>/<model>, for example `["gpt", "openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"]` (at most 4). When a request fails before any text — a busy server after 3 retries, a rate, usage or credit limit, a refused key or an expired sign-in — the turn moves to the next one and the chat shows a line "Now using …". A slot sets its own list with ai_models.<slot>.fallback. A backup with no key is skipped. |
| `ai_router` | object | `{}` | Auto model pick of plain chat turns (Default profile only): `{"mode": "auto", "quick": "quick", "deep": "main", "rules": [{"words": ["docs", "readme"], "slot": "writer"}]}`. mode auto (AI: Toggle Auto Model Pick, after a card) or off (the default). Rules come first, in order: a message that holds one of the words (whole words, any case) runs on that slot (at most 20 rules). Else a local guess, with no extra request: a short, simple message runs on quick; code, an attached file or image, a long message, think, or words like refactor, design, debug or why run on deep. The chat shows a line "Auto model: <slot> — <why>" for you only. A slot that can not run leaves the turn on main. Other profiles and agent runs keep their models. |
| `ai_concurrency` | object | `{}` | Most AI requests that run at the same time, per provider or per model: for example `{"anthropic": 2, "openai/gpt-5": 1}` (1 to 64). Chat, agent steps and ghost text all count. A request over the limit waits before it is sent; Stop ends the wait. Use it when parallel agent steps get "rate limit" (HTTP 429) answers. No entry: no limit. |
| `ai_models` | object | `{}` | Model slots for agent profiles (ai/profiles.json): slot name → `{"provider", "model", "base_url"}`, for example `{"gpt": {"provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5-mini"}}`; an optional `"reasoning"` sets the slot's reasoning level (low … max) and `"fallback"` its backup models (see ai_fallback). No keys here: a slot uses the key of its provider kind (environment variable, then AI: Configure Provider…). Built-in slots: `main` (ai_provider / ai_model, can not be replaced), `quick` (the main provider with ai_inline_model) and `local` (Ollama); a slot with the name quick or local replaces the built-in one. A bad entry is left out and named in the profile errors. |
| `ai_parallel_max` | int | `1` | How many steps of an agent profile may run at the same time (at most 8). With 1, steps run one after the other and profiles may not use `deps`. When it is not set, a planned run (a profile with a `plan` step, like the built-in plan profile) runs up to 3 steps at once. |
| `ai_dial` | object | `{}` | Changes to the effort dial (AI: Effort Dial…) by mode: low, medium, high, ultra → `{"profile", "reasoning"}`, for example `{"ultra": {"profile": "until-done"}, "low": {"reasoning": "medium"}}`. Built in: low = profile fast, think low; medium = default, medium; high = default, high; ultra = default, max. A set field replaces only that field. A mode picks the agent profile for this workspace and the reasoning level for this chat; the header chips show both. An unknown mode or level is left out and named in the errors log. |
| `ai_categories` | object | `{}` | Step categories by name, over the built-in ones (quick, deep, visual, writing, architect, ultrabrain): `{"ultrabrain": {"slot": "opus", "reasoning": "max"}, "docs": {"like": "quick", "tools": "read-only", "temperature": 0.3, "prompt_append": "Write for beginners.", "description": "user docs"}}`. slot is the model slot (else the slot of the category it is like: quick or deep, default deep); tools may narrow a step's tools (none, read-only, all); temperature is 0 to 2 (sent only to models that take it); reasoning is the level of its steps (low, medium, high, xhigh, max; the think keyword can still raise it); prompt_append joins the step's prompt; description tells the planner what it is for. A profile's own categories map wins. A bad entry is left out and named in the errors log. |
| `ai_step_escalate` | bool | `true` | A run step that is not on the deep model may answer `ESCALATE: <why>`; it then runs once more on the deep category's model, and its card says so. false: steps are not told, and such an answer stands. |
| `ai_plan_review_rounds` | int | `0` | 0: off. 1 to 5: a reviewer on the deep model reads a planner's plan and approves it, or sends its reasons back so the planner plans again, at most this many times; then the last plan goes on (plan approval still asks). Each round is one more model request. |
| `ai_plan_file` | bool | `false` | true: a planned run writes its plan to .termocode/plans/<slug>.md in the workspace: the steps with their tasks, the review rounds, the verify step's evidence and how the run ended (secrets hidden). The file shows as untracked in git unless you ignore it. false (the default): no file. |
| `ai_step_stall_minutes` | int | `10` | An agent step whose model sends nothing for this many minutes is stopped and started once more; a second stall fails the step. A running tool call (a build, a card that waits for you) is no stall. 0 turns it off; at most 120. |
| `ai_team_mode` | bool | `false` | true: agent steps that run at the same time (ai_parallel_max above 1) get team tools: team_send leaves a short note for another running step, team_claim / team_release / team_claims keep a shared list of claimed files or work, so two steps do not work on the same thing. A step's claims end with it. Notes that look like secrets are refused. Experimental; false (the default): off. |
| `ai_computer_use` | bool | `false` | true: the chat gets computer_screenshot, computer_click, computer_type and computer_key to see and use your desktop (needs xdotool and scrot on X11, grim and ydotool on Wayland, cliclick on macOS). Every action asks, with no Always allow; autopilot and allow rules never skip it. The AI can never turn this on. Experimental; false (the default): off. |
| `ai_worktrees` | enum | `auto` | auto: in a git repository, each agent step that runs at the same time as another writing step works in its own git worktree (branch termocode/agent-<id>), so they never change the same files. When it ends, its card shows the changed files with Review, Merge and Discard. off: every step works in your tree. Toggle with AI: Toggle Agent Worktrees. |
| `ai_critic` | enum | `auto` | auto: when an agent step's own git worktree (a lane) ends with changed files, a second model (the critic) reads its diff before you merge it. It gets the diff as text only (no tools; known secrets hidden). The card shows critic ok or critic: problems; Critic shows the notes, asks again or puts them in the chat box. Merge while the critic lists problems asks first (Cancel first). off: no critic review. Toggle with AI: Toggle Critic Review. |
| `ai_critic_slot` | string | `""` | The model slot the critic runs on. Empty: the other built-in model than the step's (quick for a step on main, main for every other step; main when quick is not set up). |
| `ai_plan_approval` | enum | `ask` | ask: before an agent run starts a step that changes files or runs commands, the chat shows the plan (steps, models, budget) with Deny, Approve and Edit; a read-only plan runs at once. auto: plans run without asking. always: every plan asks, read-only ones too. AI: Toggle Plan Approval turns it on or off for one chat. |
| `ai_autopilot` | enum | `off` | off: every mutating agent action asks (classes set to Always allow still run). low: read-only commands (ls, cat, grep, git status / diff / log) run without a card. medium: also file edits in the project, builds, tests and other local commands. High-risk actions always ask at every level: deletes, git push / pull, rm, sudo, network commands, writes outside the project or to .env, .git and key files. Step it with AI: Autopilot Level…; raising it asks on a card first. |
| `ai_approval_rules` | object[] | `[]` | Your own approval rules, checked before autopilot, first match wins: a list of {"tool": name or glob, "match": optional glob over the card text such as "Run: go test *", "action": allow, deny or ask}. deny refuses the call without a card; allow skips the card (not for a high-risk call); ask always shows it. |
| `ai_guardian` | string | `(none)` | A model slot (for example quick) that checks each medium-risk action autopilot would run. It answers allow or sends the action back to you with a reason on the card. It never allows what a rule denies or a high-risk action. Empty or off: no guardian. |
| `ai_compact` | enum | `auto` | auto: when a chat fills about 80% of the model's context window, or the provider says the context is too long, the older turns are summarised by the quick model (one extra request) and the chat shows "Earlier chat summarised". The model then gets the summary instead of those turns; rules, memory and todos are kept. off: never summarise (a long chat can fail with "context too long"). |
| `ai_memory_recall` | enum | `on` | While memory is on: after each AI tool call of a chat, a saved lesson about the call's file or words that this chat has not seen yet is added to the tool result and the chat shows recalled: <title> (local matching, no extra request). check: the quick model is asked first if the lesson applies (one small request per new match). off: no recall. |
| `ai_web_fetch` | bool | `false` | true gives the AI the web_fetch tool: it reads one http(s) page as text (GET only, at most 2 MB read and 20000 characters returned, no private or local addresses, secrets blanked). Turn it on in AI: Web Tools…. |
| `ai_image_gen` | bool | `false` | true gives the AI the generate_image tool when the main model is on OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: it saves one new PNG in the workspace per call. Each call is a paid request and asks first (no Always allow). Toggle with AI: Toggle Image Generation. |
| `ai_image_model` | string | `gpt-image-1` | The images model generate_image asks. It must return image data (b64_json), not a link. |
| `ai_web_search` | enum | `off` | Gives the AI the web_search tool with this provider. The key is the secret web_search_key (AI: Web Tools… → Set the search key…), else BRAVE_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY or EXA_API_KEY. A search sends the query to the provider. |
| `secret_store` | enum | `auto` | Where AI keys, sign-ins, MCP secrets and database passwords are kept. auto: the OS keyring when one answers (not over SSH, not on Termux), else an encrypted file (secrets.age, a passphrase asked once while termocode runs); never the plain file. keyring or age uses only that one (keyring with no keyring is an error, not a fallback). plain: the old ai/credentials.json (mode 0600), by choice only. An existing plain ai/credentials.json stays in use under auto until you move it (the card at start, or AI: Move Secrets to a Safer Store…). The choice is recorded in secrets.json. |
| `secret_lock_minutes` | int | `0` | Lock the encrypted secret file after this many idle minutes (0 = never; the passphrase stays until AI: Lock Secrets or quit). Each use of a secret starts the count again. Only while the file is unlocked does one timer run; none with 0, for the OS keyring or for the plain file. Read when the file is unlocked. |
| `mcp_trusted` | object | `{}` | Project MCP servers you allowed with "Always allow": server name → hash of its mcp.json entry. A changed entry asks again. Written by the trust dialog and AI: MCP Servers…. |
| `mcp_disabled_tools` | object | `{}` | MCP tools you turned off: server name → tool names. Off tools are not sent to the AI. Turn them off or on with Space in AI: MCP Servers… → a server → Show tools. |
| `mcp_channels` | array | `[]` | MCP servers that may push a message into the chat by themselves (notifications/claude/channel). The message shows as a note and a toast; it is never sent to the AI. Servers not listed here are ignored. |
| `agent_transcripts` | enum | `off` | read: termocode may read the session files that Claude Code and Codex write for themselves (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions, or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME) for Agent: Chat View, Agent: Sessions… and the search inside them. Read only: termocode never writes there. Secrets are hidden before anything is drawn, and nothing from them goes to the AI or the web panel unless you send it. A file in a format termocode does not know shows "cannot read this session". off (the default): no file there is opened. |
| `agent_auto_continue` | bool | `false` | When a Claude Code or Codex tab shows its usage-limit message, the tab is named limit ↻<time> until the reset. true: one minute after the reset, termocode types continue (then Enter) into that tab, once per limit, and a toast says so. It never types while the agent works or while a y/n or permission question is on its screen. Agent: Toggle Auto-Continue sets it for one tab. false (the default): termocode only shows the limit. |
| `agent_goal_max_tokens` | int | `0` | The token cap of a check loop (Agent: Loop Until Check Passes…): the loop stops when the agent's account used this many tokens since the loop started. Tokens are known only from the session files, so it counts only with agent_transcripts = read. 0 (the default): no token cap; the rounds and 20 minutes a round still cap the loop. |
| `agent_accounts` | object | `{}` | Named accounts of Claude Code and Codex, agent id → labels, e.g. {"claude": ["work", "personal"]}. Each account has its own config folder under termocode's config folder (agents/<agent>/<label>, only your user can open it); a tab started as that account sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CODEX_HOME to it, so the CLI keeps that sign-in there. termocode stores only the labels and never reads the sign-in files there (with agent_transcripts = read it reads only the session files, as it does in ~/.claude); it never changes ~/.claude or ~/.codex. Add one with Agent: Accounts…. |
| `agent_account_swap` | bool | `false` | Allow Agent: Switch Account… to replace the sign-in file of Claude Code (~/.claude/.credentials.json) or Codex (~/.codex/auth.json) with a saved account. The saved accounts live in the secret store; a switch shows a card (Cancel first, contents hidden), keeps the old file as <file>.termocode-backup and can be undone. Refused while an agent of that CLI runs, and not offered for Claude Code on a Mac (it keeps its sign-in in the Keychain). Off by default: Agent: Accounts… gives each account its own folder and never touches those files. |
| `agent_profiles` | object | `{}` | Launch profiles of the outside agents, agent id → list of {name, model, mode, env}, e.g. {"claude": [{"name": "review", "model": "opus", "mode": "plan"}]}. A tab started with a profile runs the CLI with its own documented flags: the model flag, the mode's permission flags (plan = read only where the CLI has it) and the env variables before it. Variables that look like secrets (KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, …) or that change which programs run (PATH, LD_*) are refused: keep keys in AI: Secret Store…. A mode without permission checks shows a card (Cancel first) at every start. Add one with Agent: Profiles…. |
| `agent_hibernate_minutes` | int | `0` | Hibernate idle Claude Code and Codex tabs: when a tab is done or waiting with no output for this many minutes, a card asks (Keep running first; Always for this session skips it later), then termocode stops the agent's program and keeps its session id (read from its session file when agent_transcripts is read). The tab stays, marked ☾. Going back to the tab types the CLI's own resume command: the same session, or the last session of the folder when no id is known. Never a tab with a question on screen or the tab you look at. Agent: Hibernate or Wake does it at once. 0 (the default): off. |
| `mcp_server_auto_approve` | object | `{}` | The "Always allow" answers you gave on an outside agent's card (see mcp_server): agent name → tool names that run without asking for that agent. Separate from ai_auto_approve, which never applies to outside agents. The name is the agent's own claim. See and revoke them in AI: Agent Auto-Approve…. |
| `mcp_trusted_tools` | object | `{}` | The tool list you trusted per MCP server: server name → hash of its tools. The first list is kept by itself; when a server's tools change, termocode asks again and, until you trust the new list, every tool of that server asks first. |

## Services (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `services_on_quit` | enum | `ask` | On quit, the Docker Compose services termocode started in this session (never the ones that were already running): ask shows a card (Keep running and quit / Stop and quit / Cancel), keep leaves them running, stop runs docker compose stop for them first. Local services always stop with the editor. |
| `services_max_log_kb` | int | `16` | Cut the log text the AI's services_logs tool returns to this many KB (the newest lines stay). |

## Web (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web_panel` | enum | `auto` | The web panel (experimental): your files, chats and terminals in a web browser. auto: Web: Open in Browser (or termocode web typed in a terminal) opens it on this computer in one step; it listens only on 127.0.0.1, with a one-time link. on: the same, and also over termocode ssh --web, and a script's termocode web --yes skips the card. off: nothing listens and the commands say it is off. Anyone who controls the browser tab can run any command as you. The AI can never open it. Applied when you save config.json. |
| `web_listen` | enum | `loopback` | Where the web panel can be reached. loopback: only on this computer (127.0.0.1), or over termocode ssh --web. tailnet: also from your own devices on your Tailscale network, at https://<this computer>.<tailnet>.ts.net/; termocode runs tailscale serve while the panel runs and refuses to start when the port is public (Funnel). Needs Tailscale with HTTPS turned on. lan: from a phone or tablet on the same Wi-Fi, no Tailscale and no cloud: https on this computer's private address (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x or 172.16-31.x.x) and web_port (47443 when not set), with a certificate made once on this computer. Pair the device with Web: Pair a Device…; the QR code carries the certificate's fingerprint, which the termocode app pins. A browser shows a certificate warning. |
| `web_require_totp` | bool | `false` | A paired phone or tablet also types a 6-digit code from an authenticator app after its passkey. Set the code up first with Web: Set Up Sign-in Code… (its key is kept in your secret store, which must be unlocked when a device signs in). The one-time link from this computer does not need it. |
| `web_app_key_login` | bool | `false` | Lets the termocode Android app pair and sign in with a key it keeps in the phone's keystore, for phones where passkeys do not work inside the app. The owner still says yes to every pairing on this computer; this computer keeps only the public key. Off: every pairing needs a passkey. |
| `web_port` | int | `0` | The port the web panel listens on, on 127.0.0.1 only. 0: a free port each time. Else 1024..65535. |
| `web_idle_minutes` | int | `15` | A browser's sign-in ends after this many minutes with no use (1..120); a paired device signs in again by itself. The panel itself stays up while termocode runs. |
| `web_max_hours` | int | `12` | A browser's sign-in ends this many hours after it began (1..24); a paired device signs in again by itself. The panel itself stays up while termocode runs. |
| `web_open_browser` | bool | `true` | Open the one-time link in the browser of this computer when the panel starts. false: only Web: Copy Link. |
| `web_max_viewers` | int | `4` | How many browsers may be connected at once (1..8). One more is turned away. |
| `web_push` | enum | `on` | on: a paired phone that turned on Notify me gets a push when the AI waits for you or a run ends and no page is open. off: no push is sent at all (the phones keep their subscription, and a later on sends again). The page's own notifications are not changed. |
| `web_push_detail` | enum | `count` | What a push to a paired phone says when something waits for you and the web page is closed (Notify me on the phone, over tailnet). none: only "Something needs you". count: how many things wait. title: the count and a fixed text for the kind (an approval, a plan, a review). Never a title, a path or a command. The push is encrypted for the phone and goes through its browser's own push service. |
| `web_phone` | enum | `off` | on: a paired phone or tablet that has the panel open keeps it running, even with its screen off, as long as its link answers. Guests and the one-time link do not. The panel stops only with Web: Stop Panel or when termocode closes. off: only real use keeps a browser's sign-in (web_idle_minutes). |
| `web_relay` | string | `(none)` | The address of a relay (https://host[:port]) that lets a paired phone reach the web panel from any network, with no VPN app. The relay only passes encrypted bytes between the laptop and the phone: both ends hold the keys (from the pairing QR code), the relay holds none and cannot read or change the panel. Empty (the default): no relay. Run your own with termocode-relay (see the web panel guide: the relay). The phone pairs with Web: Pair a Device…; its key is kept in your secret store. |
| `web_approve_on_laptop` | bool | `false` | Who confirms a web action that needs a confirm (discard changes, a delete, a database write, a command on a server). false: the paired phone or browser that asked confirms it in the page, on a card with Cancel first and the exact action; the laptop only shows a short notice. true: it waits for a card on the laptop, as before. Viewers can never act. |
| `web_projects_max` | int | `4` | How many projects a paired phone may have open at once through the web panel (1..8). The panel is the one door to every project on this computer: it joins projects that already run here, and starts one that does not run only after you say yes on a card on the laptop. One more is turned away; the phone shows Projects open now and the count. |
| `web_project_idle_minutes` | int | `60` | A project the phone opened (it was not running on the laptop) stops after this many minutes with no use from any phone (5..240). Its views then say asleep, with Open. Projects you opened yourself on the laptop never stop by this setting. |

## Appearance (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mouse_hover` | enum | `auto` | auto: the terminal reports plain pointer motion (xterm mode 1003) while termocode has focus and no text input is open, for hover labels and row highlights. off: only clicks, drags and the wheel (mode 1002), for terminals or links where motion is slow or dropped. Read at start. |
| `rtl` | enum | `auto` | Right-to-left text (Persian, Arabic, Hebrew) in the AI chat and the Markdown preview. termocode: termocode joins the letters and puts them in reading order itself, right-aligns RTL paragraphs, and asks the terminal not to reorder (BDSM, CSI 8 l). terminal: termocode sends the text unchanged and the terminal does it. off: unchanged text, no request to the terminal. auto: terminal on Konsole and mlterm (they always reorder), else termocode. Read at start. |

## Terminal (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `terminal_skip_shell` | string[] | `[]` | Actions (keymap.json names) whose keys reach termocode while the terminal has focus. Other Ctrl keys go to the shell. Quit (Ctrl+Q) and ContextHelp (Shift+F1) are in the list by default; add a name, or remove one with "-Name" (for example `["QuickOpen", "-Quit"]`). |
| `terminal_restore` | bool | `true` | After a restart of termocode, the terminal tabs of the project come back: each tab and split pane gets a fresh shell in the folder it was in, and the same tab and pane have focus. Output, scrollback and environment values are never kept. A pane that was running a program shows its name. A folder that is gone starts in the project folder. false: the panel starts empty. Read at start. |
| `terminal_restore_commands` | bool | `false` | With terminal_restore: also keep the last command line of a pane that was running a program (needs shell integration), so after a restart Enter in that pane runs it again. Command lines can hold secrets, so this is off by default; off, only the program name is kept. Read at start. |
| `terminal_shell_integration` | bool | `true` | bash, zsh and fish terminal tabs load a small script (after your own rc file) that tells termocode each command, its exit code and the folder (OSC 133 / OSC 7). It gives the tab its folder name, the "✦ Fix?" chip on a failed command and the CLI agent marks. false starts the shell exactly as before. Read when a terminal tab opens; needs Neovim 0.10+. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key. Also selects Anthropic when no provider is set. |
| `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` | Bedrock API key for the bedrock provider; wins over the saved key. |
| `AWS_REGION` | AWS region of the bedrock provider when `ai_base_url` is empty (default us-east-1). |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | Ollama host, used for the base URL of the ollama provider. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key. Also selects OpenAI when no provider is set. |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter API key. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_API_KEY` | AI API key for the selected provider; wins over saved keys. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_BASE_URL` | AI API base URL; wins over `ai_base_url`. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_MODEL` | AI chat model; wins over `ai_model`. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_PROVIDER` | AI provider; wins over `ai_provider` in config.json. |
| `TERMOCODE_FONT_DELTA` | Font size change asked of the terminal at launch (kitty with remote control only); wins over font_delta in config.json (default 0 = off). |
| `TERMOCODE_FRAME_PACING` | on / off: wait for the terminal before sending more frames, so a held key stops at once on a slow line (default: on over SSH). |
| `TERMOCODE_ICON_MODE` | Icon set: `nerd_font`, `unicode` or `ascii`. |
| `TERMOCODE_NERD_FONT` | Legacy: `1` is the same as `TERMOCODE_ICON_MODE=nerd_font`. |
| `TERMOCODE_NO_SESSION` | Any value: run without a persistent session, like `--no-session`. |
| `TERMOCODE_PLUGINS_DIR` | Folder for the Neovim plugins termocode clones on first launch. |
| `TERMOCODE_PROBE` | `off`: never ask the terminal what it can do at start (images, cell size, kitty keyboard); the environment decides. A terminal that did not answer is not asked again for 7 days (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/termocode/termcaps.json`). |
| `TERMOCODE_SYNC` | on / off: draw each frame as one (synchronized output, mode 2026), so no half-drawn frame shows on a slow link (default: on when the terminal says it supports it). |
| `TERMOCODE_TOOLS_DIR` | Folder for language servers and debug adapters installed by termocode. |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Moves the config folder to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/termocode`. |
| `XDG_DATA_HOME` | Moves the data folder to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/termocode`. |
| `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` | Folder for the persistent-session sockets (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/termocode`); without it they go to `~/.cache/termocode/sessions`. |
| `XDG_STATE_HOME` | Moves the hot-exit backups of unsaved files to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/termocode/backup` and the local history of saved files to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/termocode/history`. |
